name: GitHub
summary: Self-serve: register an OAuth app in your GitHub settings and any GitHub user can connect right away. No provider review.
scenario: An agent that reads repositories, issues and pull requests and comments on them for any GitHub user.

composio.note: Check the Composio managed OAuth directory. Composio suggests your own app for GitHub when the consent screen should show your name.

portal.accountNeeded: Any GitHub account. Create it under an organization if the app belongs to your company.

policyAndDomain.detail: A homepage URL is required, but GitHub does not verify it or ask for a privacy policy.

userCapBeforeApproval.detail: No user cap. Owners can have up to 100 OAuth apps.

adminApproval.detail: Organization owners must approve the app before members can use it on org data; new orgs restrict OAuth apps by default.

appReview.detail: The creation docs have no review or approval step. Organization owners may still need to approve the app for their org's data.

time.note: Users in organizations with OAuth app access restrictions must wait for an org owner to approve your app before it can see org repositories.

nextStep: Open GitHub Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App, and paste your callback URL (for Composio, the redirect URI shown when you create a custom auth config).

prerequisites.text: A GitHub account (personal or an organization you administer).
A public homepage URL and the exact callback URL your OAuth flow uses.

steps.title: Pick OAuth app or GitHub App
steps.detail: OAuth apps act only as the user and get broad scopes like repo. GitHub Apps give fine-grained, per-repository permissions and short-lived tokens. GitHub recommends considering a GitHub App; use an OAuth app if your auth layer only supports classic OAuth.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App. Enter app name, homepage URL, optional description and the authorization callback URL. Everything here is public.

steps.title: Add all callback URLs
steps.detail: Add up to 10 callback URLs (for example local, staging, production, or Composio's redirect URI).

steps.title: Generate and store the client secret
steps.detail: Generate a client secret and put the client ID and secret into your secret manager or your Composio custom auth config. Never commit them.

steps.title: Choose scopes in your authorize request
steps.detail: OAuth app scopes are requested at authorization time, not set in the app settings. Request the smallest set your agent needs.

steps.title: Connect your own account
steps.detail: Run the authorize flow with your account and confirm token exchange, a test API call, and refresh if token expiry is on (it is on by default).

steps.title: Tell org users about owner approval
steps.detail: New organizations restrict OAuth apps by default. Members request access from the consent flow and an org owner approves. Put this in your onboarding docs.

scopes.name: repo
scopes.purpose: Read and write private repositories, issues and pull requests.

review.summary: No GitHub review. Each organization's owners can block or approve your app for that org's data.
triggers: A user tries to access a restricted organization's resources
reviewersCheck: Org owners decide case by case; GitHub publishes no criteria for this.

blockers.issue: Agent can see personal repos but not the company's org repos.
blockers.fix: The org has OAuth app access restrictions on. The user requests access in the consent flow and an org owner approves it, or switch to a GitHub App installed on the org.
Add the exact URL (scheme, host, path) as one of the up to 10 callback URLs.

nuances.text: OAuth app scopes are coarse: repo grants access to all of a user's private repositories. A GitHub App limits access to selected repositories.
'Expire user access tokens' is on by default; your integration must handle refresh tokens or you must untick it.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app
GitHub Docs: About OAuth app access restrictions
GitHub Docs: Scopes for OAuth apps

corrections: Added org owner approval: new GitHub organizations restrict OAuth apps by default, which a 'no review' summary would hide.
